extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in analysis and PDEs studying Sobolev spaces and variational methods
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook chapter presenting definitions, fundamental properties, extension operators, Sobolev embeddings, compactness results, and characterizations of W^{m,p}, W^{1,p} and W^{1,p}_0 for use in the variational formulation of elliptic boundary value problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation of a composition (Proposition 9.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let G ∈ C1(R) with G(0)=0 and |G'(s)| ≤ M ∀s ∈ R. Let u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) with 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞. Then G ◦ u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) and ∂_i(G◦u) = (G'◦u) ∂_i u, i=1,...,N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses dominated convergence and approximation by C^∞_c functions when 1 ≤ p < ∞; for p=∞ reduce to the finite-p case on compact support. Also notes |G(s)| ≤ M|s| implies G◦u ∈ L^p and (G'◦u)∂_i u ∈ L^p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of variables formula in W^{1,p} (Proposition 9.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Ω and Ω̃ be open in R^N and H: Ω̃ → Ω a bijection with H ∈ C1(Ω̃), H^{-1} ∈ C1(Ω), Jac H ∈ L^∞(Ω̃), Jac H^{-1} ∈ L^∞(Ω). If u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) (1 ≤ p ≤ ∞) then u◦H ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω̃) and ∂_{y_j} u(H(y)) = Σ_i (∂_{x_i} u)(H(y)) ∂_{y_j} H_i(y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by approximating u with C^∞_c and pulling back; L^p convergence of gradients uses boundedness of Jacobians. Similar for p=∞ via reduction to finite-p on compact sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of W^{m,p}(Ω)
rubrics_metrics.description: W^{m,p}(Ω) defined inductively: u ∈ W^{m,p} iff u ∈ W^{m-1,p} and ∂_i u ∈ W^{m-1,p} ∀i, equivalently u ∈ L^p and for all multi-indices α with |α| ≤ m there exist g_α ∈ L^p s.t. ∫_Ω u D^α ϕ = (-1)^{|α|} ∫_Ω g_α ϕ for all ϕ ∈ C^∞_c(Ω). Set D^α u = g_α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equip with norm ||u||_{W^{m,p}} = (Σ_{0≤|α|≤m} ||D^α u||_p^p)^{1/p} (or sup for p=∞). W^{m,p} is a Banach space; H^m = W^{m,2} is a Hilbert space with inner product Σ_{|α|≤m} (D^α u, D^α v)_{L^2}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of norms on W^{m,p} for smooth bounded domains (Remark 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is 'smooth enough' with ∂Ω bounded, the W^{m,p} norm is equivalent to ||u||_p + Σ_{|α|=m} ||D^α u||_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More precisely, for every multi-index α with 0<|α|<m and every ε>0 there exists C (depending on Ω, ε, α) s.t. ||D^α u||_p ≤ ε Σ_{|β|=m} ||D^β u||_p + C||u||_p ∀u∈W^{m,p}(Ω). Reference: R. Adams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of linear extension operator P (Theorem 9.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is of class C^1 with ∂Ω bounded (or Ω=R^N_+), there exists a linear operator P: W^{1,p}(Ω) → W^{1,p}(R^N) (1 ≤ p ≤ ∞) such that (i) P u|_Ω = u, (ii) ||P u||_{L^p(R^N)} ≤ C ||u||_{L^p(Ω)}, (iii) ||P u||_{W^{1,p}(R^N)} ≤ C ||u||_{W^{1,p}(Ω)}, with C depending only on Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed by local charts, partition of unity, reflection extensions on Q+, and patching; used repeatedly to transfer results from R^N to Ω.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension by reflection on Q+ (Lemma 9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given u ∈ W^{1,p}(Q+) define ũ on Q by reflection: ũ(x',x_N)=u(x',x_N) for x_N>0 and u(x',-x_N) for x_N<0. Then ũ ∈ W^{1,p}(Q) and ||ũ||_{L^p(Q)} ≤ 2 ||u||_{L^p(Q+)}, ||ũ||_{W^{1,p}(Q)} ≤ 2 ||u||_{W^{1,p}(Q+)}. Derivatives reflect with signs: ∂_{x_i} ũ = (∂_{x_i} u)̃ for i=1,...,N-1, ∂_{x_N} ũ = (∂_{x_N} u)̃ with sign change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses test-function approximation with cutoff η_k and dominated convergence; provides a simple extension construction used in Theorem 9.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partition of unity (Lemma 9.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given compact K⊂R^N and an open cover U_1,...,U_k of K, there exist θ_0, θ_1,...,θ_k ∈ C^∞(R^N) with 0 ≤ θ_i ≤ 1, Σ_{i=0}^k θ_i = 1 on R^N, supp θ_i compact and supp θ_i ⊂ U_i for i≥1, and supp θ_0 ⊂ R^N \ K. If Ω is bounded and K=∂Ω then θ_0|_Ω ∈ C^∞_c(Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classical construction used to localize arguments and build global extension operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of C^∞_c restrictions (Corollary 9.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is C^1 and u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) with 1 ≤ p < ∞, there exists a sequence (u_n) from C^∞_c(R^N) with u_n|_Ω → u in W^{1,p}(Ω). Equivalently, restrictions of C^∞_c(R^N) are dense in W^{1,p}(Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses the extension operator P and mollification/cutoff; for unbounded ∂Ω use truncation ζ_n u and then extend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sobolev embedding in R^N (Theorem 9.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1 ≤ p < N, W^{1,p}(R^N) ⊂ L^{p*}(R^N) where 1/p* = 1/p - 1/N, and there exists C=C(p,N) such that ||u||_{p*} ≤ C ||∇u||_p for all u ∈ W^{1,p}(R^N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof begins with p=1 using one-dimensional integral estimates and Lemma 9.4, then obtains general p by applying the p=1 case to |u|^{m-1}u and choosing m appropriately; scaling argument shows p* is the unique exponent compatible with scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-integrability lemma (Lemma 9.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f_i ∈ L^{N-1}(R^{N-1}), i=1,...,N, and define f(x)=Π_{i=1}^N f_i(˜x_i) (where ˜x_i omits x_i), then f ∈ L^1(R^N) and ||f||_{L^1(R^N)} ≤ Π_{i=1}^N ||f_i||_{L^{N-1}(R^{N-1})}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the p=1 Sobolev embedding proof; proved by induction and Hölder/Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpolation and L^q embeddings (Corollary 9.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 1 ≤ p < N and p ≤ q ≤ p*, then W^{1,p}(R^N) ⊂ L^q(R^N) with continuous injection and ||u||_q ≤ C ||u||_{W^{1,p}}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain q between p and p* by interpolation: 1/q = α/p + (1-α)/p* and apply Young/Holder inequalities together with Theorem 9.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting case p=N embeddings (Corollary 9.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: For p=N, W^{1,N}(R^N) ⊂ L^q(R^N) for every finite q ∈ [N,∞), with continuous injection (constants blow up as q→∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: iterate the inequality applied to powers and use interpolation to extend to all finite q; density extends to W^{1,N}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morrey's theorem (Theorem 9.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p>N then W^{1,p}(R^N) ⊂ L^∞(R^N) and there is a continuous embedding; moreover functions have Hölder continuous representatives: |u(x)-u(y)| ≤ C |x-y|^{α} ||∇u||_p a.e., with α = 1 - N/p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by estimating deviation from the mean on cubes and applying Hölder; yields continuity representative and uniform estimates. Also implies lim_{|x|→∞} u(x)=0 when N<p<∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-order Sobolev embeddings (Corollary 9.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: For integer m≥1 and 1 ≤ p < ∞: W^{m,p}(R^N) ⊂ L^q(R^N) where 1/q = 1/p - m/N if 1/p - m/N >0; if equal to 0 then W^{m,p} ⊂ L^q ∀q∈[p,∞); if <0 then W^{m,p} ⊂ L^∞. If m - N/p >0 non-integer, set k=[m - N/p], θ=m - N/p - k ∈ (0,1); then D^α u ∈ L^∞ for |α| ≤ k and D^α u are Hölder continuous of exponent θ for |α|=k; in particular W^{m,p} ⊂ C^k(R^N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtained by iterated application of the W^{1,p} embedding results (Theorem 9.9, Corollary 9.11, Morrey).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local/domain Sobolev embeddings (Corollary 9.14 & 9.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω⊂R^N is C^1 with bounded boundary (or Ω=R^N_+), the same embeddings as on R^N hold for W^{1,p}(Ω): W^{1,p}(Ω) ⊂ L^{p*}(Ω) for p<N, ⊂ L^q(Ω) ∀q∈[p,∞) for p=N, ⊂ L^∞(Ω) and C(Ω) for p>N. Higher-order results (Corollary 9.13) extend to Ω (Corollary 9.15) under appropriate smoothness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the extension operator P to reduce to the whole-space case; constants depend on Ω.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rellich–Kondrachov compactness (Theorem 9.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is bounded and C^1, then the embeddings W^{1,p}(Ω) → L^q(Ω) are compact for q ∈ [1,p*) (with 1/p* = 1/p - 1/N) when p<N; for p=N compact into L^q for any q∈[p,∞), and for p>N compact into C(Ω). In particular W^{1,p}(Ω) compactly embeds into L^p(Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to whole-space estimates via an extension P and verifies translation-compactness by interpolation and gradient control; comments on optimality and failure of compactness for unbounded domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of mixed norms (Remark 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: For bounded C^1 Ω, the norm |||u||| = ||∇u||_p + ||u||_q is equivalent to the W^{1,p} norm provided q lies in the permitted range: 1 ≤ q ≤ p* if p < N; 1 ≤ q < ∞ if p = N; 1 ≤ q ≤ ∞ if p > N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for alternative norm choices in functional settings; follows from embedding results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trudinger inequality and borderline remarks (Remark 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: When p=N, W^{1,N}(Ω) functions need not be bounded (counterexample u(x)=(log(1/|x|))^α near 0). Nevertheless Trudinger's inequality holds: ∫_Ω exp(|u|^{N/(N-1)}) < ∞ for all u ∈ W^{1,N}(Ω). Also W^{N,1} ⊂ L^∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights the special 'limiting' behaviour at p=N and references for detailed proofs (R. Adams, Gilbarg–Trudinger).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and basic properties of W^{1,p}_0(Ω)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1 ≤ p < ∞, W^{1,p}_0(Ω) denotes the closure of C^1_c(Ω) in W^{1,p}(Ω). H^1_0(Ω)=W^{1,2}_0(Ω). W^{1,p}_0 is separable Banach; reflexive if 1<p<∞; in R^N we have W^{1,p}_0(R^N)=W^{1,p}(R^N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions in W^{1,p}_0 intuitively 'vanish on ∂Ω'; precise characterizations follow (Theorem 9.17, Proposition 9.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactly supported functions belong to W^{1,p}_0 (Lemma 9.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) with supp u compactly contained in Ω, then u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: multiply by cutoff α∈C^1_c(ω) (α=1 on supp u) and approximate by smooth functions in ω; used to build W^{1,p}_0 elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of W^{1,p}_0 via boundary vanishing (Theorem 9.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ω is C^1 and u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) ∩ C(Ω) (1 ≤ p < ∞), then u = 0 on ∂Ω iff u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(Ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses truncations and approximation for (i)⇒(ii); converse reduced by local charts to showing functions in W^{1,p}_0(Q+) must vanish on Q_0 using approximations and integral estimates. Smoothness of Ω is required for (ii)⇒(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of W^{1,p}_0 (Proposition 9.18)
rubrics_metrics.description:
For Ω of class C^1 and 1<p<∞, for u∈L^p(Ω) the following are equivalent: (i) u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(Ω); (ii) there exists C such that |∫_Ω u ∂_i ϕ| ≤ C ||ϕ||_{L^{p^*}(Ω)} for all ϕ ∈ C^1_c(R^N), i=1,...,N (i.e., u defines a bounded functional on gradients); (iii) the zero extension 
bar{u} (u on Ω, 0 outside) belongs to W^{1,p}(R^N) (then ∂_i 
bar{u} = extension of ∂_i u).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implications: (i)⇒(ii) via approximating sequences; (ii)⇒(iii) gives control to show extension belongs to whole-space Sobolev; (iii)⇒(i) uses mollifiers supported in positive half to construct approximations inside Ω.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poincaré inequality on bounded domains (Corollary 9.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 1 ≤ p < ∞ and Ω is bounded, there exists C(Ω,p) such that ||u||_{L^p(Ω)} ≤ C ||∇u||_{L^p(Ω)} for all u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(Ω). Consequently ||∇u||_{L^p} is a norm on W^{1,p}_0(Ω) equivalent to the full W^{1,p} norm; for H^1_0 the gradient inner product induces an equivalent norm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poincaré remains true when Ω has finite measure or bounded projection on some axis. Proof follows from compactness/density and embedding results.
